dedupe_keys.name: wfp sdi t logistics database layers global bridges border crossing points and obstacles

description: These three global point layers come from the Logistics Database of WFP's Spatial Data Infrastructure for Transport (SDI-T), maintained by the World Food Programme with the Logistics Cluster for humanitarian operations and shared on the Humanitarian Data Exchange. Global bridges records bridge name, type (arch, beam, truss, floating, suspension, culvert), status, damage, length, maximum declared load in tonnes, estimated crossing time, practicability, surface, bypass and location precision. Global border crossing points records status, customs presence and the two countries at each crossing. Global obstacles records roadblocks, floods, mines, road, railway, bridge and culvert damage, checkpoints, traffic restrictions, landslides and fords with an observation date and maximum load. Each layer is offered as a shapefile and GeoJSON with an attribute metadata file, under CC BY-SA, free on HDX. The metadata are dated October 2014 and the files were last modified between 2017 and 2020; no update schedule is given. Caveats: coverage is limited to countries where WFP operated, blank or zero attributes mean no data, location precision ranges from GPS to "bad", and obstacle records describe conditions at their observation date only. The layers support emergency response and logistics network studies such as routing relief convoys around damaged bridges and closed crossings; related records are HIFLD Open and the World Port Index.
